To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a glycosylation-dependent recombinant sub-unit candidate vaccine consisting of the immunodominant Ehrlichia major antigenic protein 1 induced a protective immune response in a susceptible animal model.
we have shown, for the first, time that the major antigenic protein of E. ruminantitype is a glycosylation-dependent antigen that induces protective immunity against heartwater disease in sheep.

the glycosylation status of the MAP1 antigen is an important determinant for its immunogenicity and that a glycosylized MAP1 subunit vaccine candidate is a promising DIVA vaccine candidate for use in heartwater endemic and non-endemic areas.
